lines.text: About ten seconds after this earthquake, the side of a mountain began to slide away.
Mount St. Helens. 8:32 in the morning, the eighteenth of May, 1980.
And the quake was only a magnitude five point one.
Put that next to the largest earthquake in United States history. That one released about one point four million times the energy.
Draw them both to scale, and the five point one is a square too small to see.
And yet the slide released the pressure, and the volcano erupted.
So what was already inside that mountain? That's magnitude five, and the full video is linked right here.
